newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees Rank Xerox deal adding to EPS.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees Rank Xerox deal adding to EPS.

text.p: Xerox Corp on Friday said it expected its buyout of the Rank Group Plc's remaining stake in the Rank Xerox joint venture to add $0.10 a share to the company's fiscal 1997's earnings.
Xerox spokesman Judd Everhart told Reuters in an interview that the company raised its 1997 earnings target from $3.85 per share to $3.95.

Everhart said the purchase of Rank's 20 percent stake in the office equipment venture should add $0.20 per share to fiscal 1998 earnings. The First Call consensus estimate for 1998 had been $4.35 per share.
The Rank Xerox venture contributed $432 million to Xerox's net income of $1.2 billion in fiscal 1996, Everhart said.
Xerox formed the joint venture in 1956 and has controlled it since 1969, he said. "We decided to take more over the years," Everhart said.
Rank had been eager to sell its remaining stake as part of its effort to focus on its core restaurant and entertainment business, Rank and Xerox officials told Reuters in separate interviews.

Recognizing Rank's willingness to sell, it was just a matter of price, Everhart said. "It was strictly the price," he said. "The price was attractive and we were confident it will not hurt our bottom line."
Wall Street analysts agreed the price was right, and several moved quickly to raise their earnings estimates.
Salomon Brothers Inc estimated that Xerox paid about 10 times 1997 earnings for the remaining 20 percent, funding the acquisition through free cash flow.
"The price was consistent with the 13 percent stake they added from Rank in 1995," said Rudy Hokanson of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. In 1995, Xerox raised its stake from 67 percent to 80 percent.
"This was a real opportunity to enhance shareholder value," he said.
Jack Kelly of Goldman Sachs said he had raised Xerox's stock price target to $80 per share from $75 based on the news. The stock was up 7/8 at midday to 67-1/2.

Everhart said that when Xerox suspended its $1 billion share-buyback program Friday, it had acquired more than $400 million, or about 2.8 million shares. The buyback was suspended because of the Rank buyout.
